---
title: Candidate assessment specification
---

`cand_assessment` is an immutable, pipeline-compatible diagnostic card. It returns
its incoming reactive source without gating downstream export on its task or
settings. No Apply action, pipeline step or final full-data fit is introduced.

`candidate_assessment.selection` prefers the current `proxy_data.ensemble_results`.
An active ensemble pipeline with stale runtime evidence waits rather than falling
back. Otherwise it requires a compatible, nonhistorical completed weighted winner
in `tuning_results.review.winner_trial`. Missing winners wait. The assessment
signature includes only the selected pipeline/trial and relevant source context;
unrelated search publications do not restart collection.

`assess_candidate` uses `prepare` to regenerate individual-model splits and fixed
settings from the reviewed seed and current evaluation plan. Native session cache
keys match training keys. Missing individual artifacts are fitted sequentially
under the session's ensemble-priority leases with cooperative cancellation between
folds. Fit failures remain visible. Private cache pins are released in a finally
block; no fitted objects or row-level predictions are added to portable evidence.
Browser execution uses the existing sequential memory service.

Committed ensembles use their stored split-fitted members, with cached member
responses where available. Responses are combined using the committed aggregation
style. Hard voting additionally produces per-class member vote fractions as
ranking scores, without exposing them as probabilities or changing predictions.
Probabilities and decision scores are aligned by class; pairwise OVO decision
columns are not interpreted as per-class scores. Labels-only classifiers use a
confusion matrix. Validation predictions retain positional source-row and split
identity, including duplicate dataframe indices and repeated validation appearances.

Regression displays actual versus predicted values on equally scaled square axes,
a 1:1 reference and empirical P2.5/P97.5 signed-error offset lines. At most 5,000
prediction events are plotted deterministically; references and statistics use all
events. Error is predicted minus actual, variance has denominator N. Pooled-event
RMSE, MAE, R², bias, variance and percentiles are reported overall and by group.
Constant-target R² is unavailable.

Classification ROC is computed within splits for the selected class versus rest,
then interpolated and averaged on a fixed false-positive-rate grid. Split AUC means,
sample SDs and usable counts are reported. Single-outcome or incomplete-score splits
are excluded explicitly. The confusion matrix uses percentages within actual
classes, with counts on hover and a group selector. Classification probability-error
bias, population variance and selected-class Brier score require probability outputs;
vote shares and decisions do not qualify. Accuracy metrics describe pooled events.

Colour and symbol controls offer Stratifier and Sensitive variables only. Numeric
variables with more than five values use up to five quantile bins; categorical
variables retain twelve most common levels plus Other, with Missing separate.
Different controls produce intersection groups. Display controls and fullscreen do
not affect fit collection. Dynamic controls preserve valid restored values.

Background results are accepted only for the current signature. Cancellation signals
superseded tasks; sessions stop their work and release resources. Persistent widget
updates follow `WidgetSlot` and `update_figure`. The front and table explicitly
describe post-selection resampling rather than independent test performance.

Tests cover waiting/selection, committed-ensemble precedence and stale detection,
training-artifact reuse, repeated memberships and positional alignment, grouped
error moments, vote-share ROC, labels-only fallback, absent classes, references,
cancellation, restoration, pass-through exports and display-only UI changes.
